policy.root_cause_rule: Do not mark a likely cause as confirmed until the case-specific confirmation evidence is present.

corrections.resolution: Stop or correct the abnormal log source, preserve required logs, validate a logrotate rule with logrotate -d, and reclaim space only under the retention and change policy.
corrections.safety: Do not delete an open log or truncate evidence without approval; a deleted-open file may continue consuming blocks until its process closes it.

corrections.resolution: Collect process and application evidence, remove or reject the malformed workload when possible, and use an approved service restart only as temporary recovery. Apply the application fix for permanent resolution.
corrections.safety: Do not kill the process before identifying the owning service and transaction impact.

corrections.resolution: Capture a workload-normalized memory trend and vendor diagnostics before recovery. Restart only with approval, then deploy the vendor or application fix and confirm that RSS no longer grows under comparable load.
corrections.safety: Low available memory alone is not proof of a leak because Linux uses memory for cache.

corrections.corrected_root_cause: The persistent mount entry referenced an identifier that no longer resolved after the approved storage change, while the expected logical volume and filesystem were otherwise healthy.
corrections.resolution: Back up /etc/fstab, correct the entry using the verified filesystem UUID or supported device-mapper path, run findmnt --verify, and test only the intended mount point.
corrections.safety: Do not create a filesystem or run filesystem repair until the device identity and data ownership are confirmed.

corrections.corrected_title: SSSD domain authentication failure caused by a broken AD machine-account trust
corrections.resolution: After proving DNS, time and DC connectivity are healthy, repair or update the machine trust using the approved directory-services procedure. Rejoin the domain only if the supported repair fails.
corrections.safety: Preserve a tested local administrative access path before changing domain membership or SSSD state.

corrections.resolution: Restore the network path or resolver service. If a resolver change is approved, apply it through the active NetworkManager connection and verify persistence.
corrections.safety: Do not replace enterprise DNS with a public resolver or permanent hosts-file workaround.

corrections.corrected_title: SSH gateway access failure caused by an expired TLS certificate on the gateway
corrections.corrected_scope: The certificate terminates TLS on the access gateway; it is not an OpenSSH user or host certificate.
corrections.resolution: Issue a replacement from the approved CA, validate subject/SAN, chain, private-key association and validity, deploy through the gateway's supported procedure, reload only the affected component, and test a new session.
corrections.rollback: Retain the prior certificate and configuration until validation completes, then restore them if the gateway fails health checks.
corrections.safety: If the environment actually uses OpenSSH certificates, validate them with ssh-keygen -L -f <certificate>, not openssl x509.

corrections.resolution: Determine whether failure is local cache, entitlement, proxy/TLS, reachability or published metadata. Correct the responsible layer and retry a metadata refresh before the patch transaction.
corrections.safety: Do not disable TLS verification or repository signature checking.

corrections.resolution: Restore reachability to the approved time source and allow chronyd to converge. Use chronyc makestep only when the offset and application impact have been assessed and approval is recorded.
corrections.safety: A backward or large forward time step can affect databases, clusters, schedulers and audit logs.

diagnostics: Vendor backup-console capacity, job and retention reports
corrections.resolution: Restore capacity by extending the approved repository or expiring data through the backup product's supported retention workflow, then rerun and verify a backup and restore test.
corrections.safety: Never remove repository files directly from the operating system unless the backup vendor explicitly supports it.

corrections.resolution: Correct the syntax in the owning crontab, preserve the previous entry, confirm the execution user and environment, and test the command non-destructively under that identity.
corrections.safety: Files in /etc/cron.d include a user field; per-user crontabs do not. Do not copy syntax between them unchanged.

corrections.resolution: Archive or remove only logs beyond the approved retention period, then configure IIS rollover plus an approved archival/compression or scheduled-retention process.
corrections.safety: Preserve security, legal and troubleshooting evidence; do not disable IIS logging to recover space.

corrections.resolution: Correct the confirmed failed dependency or its configuration, start it under change control, then start and validate the dependent application service.
corrections.safety: Do not change service dependencies in the registry without a documented vendor configuration and rollback.

corrections.resolution: Use console or approved remote management to correct the confirmed service, listener, firewall or policy fault. Start TermService only when it is unexpectedly stopped and its dependencies are healthy.
corrections.safety: Restarting Remote Desktop Services can disconnect active users; announce impact and obtain approval.

diagnostics: Record the exact Windows Update error and KB
Review Setup and WindowsUpdateClient event logs
corrections.resolution: Follow the Microsoft procedure that matches the confirmed SRP/EFI layout and update error. Back up boot configuration and prepare tested recovery media before any partition or boot-file change.
corrections.safety: Treat partition resizing or deletion of SRP/EFI content as high risk; generic Disk Management instructions are insufficient.

corrections.resolution: Confirm the scanner contribution, use built-in/server-role exclusions where applicable, and add only the smallest vendor-supported custom exclusion after security approval.
corrections.safety: Do not disable real-time protection as a test. Broad path, process or extension exclusions create material security exposure.

diagnostics: Get-Counter '\Hyper-V Hypervisor Logical Processor(*)\% Total Run Time'
Get-Counter '\Hyper-V Hypervisor Virtual Processor(*)\% Guest Run Time'
corrections.resolution: Confirm sustained host contention and the responsible workload, then use approved workload throttling, right-sizing, capacity addition or live migration. Validate every affected guest after rebalancing.
corrections.safety: Do not use guest Task Manager alone to infer physical CPU saturation, and do not call the Hyper-V metric CPU ready.

corrections.resolution: After DNS, time and DC connectivity checks pass, run Test-ComputerSecureChannel -Repair with approved domain credentials. Remove/rejoin only if supported repair fails.
corrections.safety: Confirm local or console administrative access before trust repair. Do not reset the computer account blindly on a domain controller.

corrections.scope_rule: Use only when failures are reproduced from multiple network segments and both Linux and Windows against the shared enterprise DNS service.
corrections.resolution: Invoke the DNS major-incident procedure, restore authoritative/recursive service or approved failover, and validate representative records from both platforms and segments.
corrections.safety: Avoid mass local resolver or hosts-file changes that hide an enterprise DNS failure.

corrections.scope_rule: Use only when a shared authoritative time source or hierarchy affects multiple hosts on both platforms.
diagnostics: Compare offsets against the approved authoritative source
corrections.resolution: Restore the enterprise time hierarchy or approved failover, allow controlled convergence, and validate Kerberos only after offsets return within policy.
corrections.safety: Do not force-step clocks fleet-wide without assessing database, clustering, token, scheduler and audit-log impact.
